title: Keyboard Manager sequence-to-text mapping uses paste in protected fields

status.label: Confirm sequence input behavior on current release
status.detail: A shortcut sequence reportedly inserts text by paste, which is blocked by password fields and SSH terminals; current-version behavior is unconfirmed.

judgment.rationale: The reporter lists PowerToys 0.98.1 and says a Ctrl+` E sequence used to type text character-by-character but now behaves like Ctrl+V, which a protected third-party password field blocks. Another user confirms the paste behavior is incompatible with SSH terminals. The report requests a choice between pasting text and emitting keystrokes; no current-version confirmation is present.
evidence: The report lists PowerToys 0.98.1 from WinGet on Windows 11 Pro 25H2 with Polish locale.
The reporter says the Ctrl+` E sequence previously typed the target text but now behaves like Ctrl+V in a third-party password field.
A second user confirms the behavior is a Ctrl+V operation and says it is incompatible with SSH terminals.
The reporter does not disclose the third-party application name; the report has no diagnostic attachment.
judgment.recommended_action: Ask whether current stable still emits paste for the sequence action and whether an explicit keystroke-sequence option would cover the use case; do not ask for the protected app name or password contents.

fix_assessment.rationale: The reporter and a second user describe paste-based output as incompatible with protected fields and SSH terminals. A separate keystroke-sequence mode could preserve the existing paste behavior while supporting targets that block paste, but the latest version behavior and desired configuration are unconfirmed.

proposed_fixes.title: Offer keystroke-sequence output alongside paste-based text insertion
proposed_fixes.root_cause: The new Keyboard Manager sequence action appears to emit its text through the clipboard/paste path, which protected fields and some SSH terminals reject. The report asks for a choice between paste and character-by-character input.
plan: Confirm the current editor's output mode for sequence-to-text mappings and the exact behavior in a protected field or SSH terminal.
Add an explicit output choice if the current behavior is paste-only: paste text or emit a keystroke sequence.
Preserve the current paste mode as the default unless product requirements specify otherwise.
Add focused tests for both modes and a target that blocks clipboard paste.
verification: Verify paste mode continues to insert text in ordinary editable fields.
Verify keystroke-sequence mode types the configured characters into a protected field or SSH terminal that blocks Ctrl+V.
Verify no password or other sensitive text is included in diagnostics or logs.

confidence.rationale: Two users confirm paste-based behavior and the requested alternative is clear, but current-version behavior and product support expectations are unverified.

issue_context.summary: A Keyboard Manager sequence reportedly pastes text with Ctrl+V instead of emitting individual keystrokes, so protected password fields and SSH terminals reject it.
known_information: The report lists PowerToys 0.98.1 from WinGet on Windows 11 Pro 25H2.
The configured Ctrl+` E sequence reportedly used to type text and now behaves like Ctrl+V.
A second user confirms the paste operation is incompatible with SSH terminals.
The original reporter intentionally does not disclose the protected third-party application name.
inferences: The new editor may use clipboard paste for sequence text, but an explicit current-build comparison is still needed.
issue_context.analysis: The requested behavior is a choice of output mechanism rather than a request to bypass a specific application's security. Keep the report's privacy boundary: do not ask for the app name or any password contents.
initial_investigation: Read the full issue and follow-up, including the exact sequence, versions, protected-field behavior, SSH confirmation, labels, and absence of diagnostics.
No linked fix or cross-reference was found.

information_gaps.information: Whether current stable still performs paste for sequence-to-text mappings and whether a selectable keystroke-sequence mode would resolve the reported use case
information_gaps.why_needed: This determines whether the behavior is still present and confirms the desired distinction between paste and character-by-character output.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: On current stable, test the sequence in a safe non-sensitive protected field or SSH terminal and report whether it pastes or types characters. Do not share the application name, password, or sensitive text.

comment.body: Thanks for describing the sequence and the protected-field limitation; the SSH follow-up also confirms that paste is not equivalent to typing characters. Could you confirm whether current stable still performs a Ctrl+V-style paste for this mapping, and whether a selectable keystroke-sequence mode would address the problem? Please do not share the application name, password, or any sensitive text.
